title: Manage AI cost and speed, and decide when to fine-tune
summary: Every AI call costs money and takes time. Estimate both early, pick the cheapest model that meets the quality bar, and use simple savings before anything complex.

beginner: Learn that cost depends on how much text goes in and comes out.
Estimate calls per user per day and the cost per call.
Multiply out to a monthly cost at your expected usage.
Agree how fast a response must be for the feature to feel usable.
Set a spending cap before launch.
intermediate: Compare models on quality, speed and cost with your own test set.
Use savings such as caching repeated instructions and batching non-urgent work.
Decide whether fine-tuning is worth it only after simpler options.
experienced: Set cost and speed targets for AI features across products.
Build unit economics into pricing and business cases.
Review model choices regularly, because prices and models change quickly.

canDelegateTo.task: Compare models on quality and speed

toolExamples.aws: Set billing alerts for AI usage.
toolExamples.gcp: Set a budget alert on the AI project.
toolExamples.claude: Check current model pricing before you estimate.

definitionOfDone: Model chosen against a test set
pitfalls: Using the largest model by default
